title_en: Fang Jinkai v. Tong'an Hospital — dispute over medical damage compensation
keywords_en: Civil; Medical damage compensation dispute; First instance; Basic People's Court; Fujian Province; Natural person; Legal person; General Principles of Civil Law; Risk disclosure and consent for medical treatment; Causal relationship between medical conduct and damage consequences; Validity of medical accident appraisal conclusions; Dismissal of claims; Twisting injury of left calf; Open fracture; Wound infection; Osteomyelitis; Shortening of left leg; Assumption of risk; Tong'an Hospital medical damage compensation dispute
full_text_en:
Fang Jinkai v. Tong'an Hospital — Dispute over Medical Damage Compensation

[Ruling Summary]

If a risky medical procedure is carried out with the consent of the patient and his or her relatives, the risk liability shall be borne by the patient and his or her relatives.

Plaintiff: Fang Jinkai, male, 33 years old, residing in Lianhua Town, Tong'an District, Xiamen City, Fujian Province.

Defendant: Tong'an Hospital of Xiamen City, Fujian Province, domiciled at Datong Town, Tong'an District, Xiamen City, Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Gongyang, President of the Hospital.

The plaintiff, Fang Jinkai, filed a lawsuit with the Tong'an District People's Court of Xiamen City, Fujian Province, against the defendant, Tong'an Hospital of Xiamen City, Fujian Province (hereinafter referred to as Tong'an Hospital), over a dispute concerning medical damage compensation.

Plaintiff's Allegations: I was admitted to the First Department of Surgery of the defendant hospital after my left leg was mangled by a mixer. Because the defendant's doctors failed to operate in accordance with standard procedures, they did not thoroughly clean and disinfect the泥沙 (sediment) in the wound, which led to infection and resulted in osteomyelitis and bone necrosis. Subsequently, when the defendant performed a bone graft surgery on me, it caused my left leg to be 4 cm shorter than my right leg, leaving me permanently disabled. The defendant was at fault in the course of treating me and should be liable for compensation according to law. I request the court to order the defendant to compensate me for lost work income of RMB 48,374, medical expenses of RMB 19,915.38, disability living subsidy of RMB 33,834, and mental distress damages of RMB 5,639, totaling RMB 107,762.38.

The plaintiff, Fang Jinkai, submitted the medical records and surgical records from the Navy Tong'an Minhai Hospital of the People's Liberation Army (hereinafter referred to as Minhai Hospital), as well as the Forensic Clinical Examination Report No. (2002) Xiamen Zhongfa Fayi Zi 148 issued by the Judicial Technical Appraisal Division of the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court, to prove that after the surgery performed by Tong'an Hospital, there was still coal sediment in his wound, and that his left lower limb was shortened by 3.3 cm, with a disability grade of Level 9 plus Level 10.

Defendant's Defense: When the plaintiff came to our hospital for treatment, he had an open comminuted fracture of the lower left leg, with a large amount of coal cinders, sediment, and other contaminants attached to the wound. Given the severity of his injury, the best way to completely avoid post-operative infection would have been amputation, but that would have certainly left the plaintiff permanently disabled. In order to minimize the plaintiff's loss, our hospital decided to adopt a surgical approach involving wound debridement, internal fixation with a steel plate, and external fixation with a plaster cast, in an effort to save the leg. However, this approach carried the risk of wound infection and concurrent osteomyelitis. Our hospital was fully aware of these consequences, and therefore, before the surgery, we informed the plaintiff and his relatives of the surgical risks, and the surgery proceeded only after the plaintiff's relatives signed a consent form. During the surgery, although the medical staff irrigated the wound with three 500 ml bottles of hydrogen peroxide and fifteen 500 ml bottles of normal saline for external use, the nature of the plaintiff's injury made it impossible for the hospital to completely clean the wound in a single procedure. After the first surgery, the plaintiff failed to cooperate with treatment and requested discharge before the risk period for surgery had passed. Two months later, the plaintiff was readmitted to our hospital for the second time due to severe open compound injury of the left leg with infection, and fracture of the left tibia and fibula with osteomyelitis. Our hospital performed an incision expansion, fracture reduction and fixation, and bone grafting. After surgery, comprehensive treatments including anti-inflammatory therapy and drainage were administered, and the wound healed, leading to discharge. Over a month later, the plaintiff was hospitalized for a third time. During this admission, physical examination revealed that the external fixator on the plaintiff's left leg had loosened, and the left leg was deformed with an inward angulation, indicating that the plaintiff had engaged in excessive activity after discharge, resulting in a re-fracture. This time, our hospital administered anti-inflammatory and infusion therapy, changed the external fixation to a plaster cast fixation, and the wound improved. Because the plaintiff developed osteomyelitis and bone necrosis, the bone ends at the fracture site overlapped by about 3 cm. The newly grafted bone could only reinforce the area but could not separate the overlapped portions, ultimately making the left leg unavoidably shorter than the right. All of our hospital's diagnoses and treatments for the plaintiff were in compliance with standard procedures; there were no operations that violated the rules. The plaintiff's disability was caused by the mixer injury, not by the medical treatment. After appraisal by both the district-level and municipal-level medical accident appraisal committees, the plaintiff's disability was determined not to be a medical accident. His claims lack a legal basis and should be dismissed.

The defendant, Tong'an Hospital, submitted the medical records from the plaintiff Fang Jinkai's three hospitalizations and the X-ray films from the third hospitalization, to prove that before the first surgery, Fang Jinkai and his relatives had been informed of the surgical risks; that after Fang Jinkai underwent surgery at another hospital, there were still irremovable contaminants in his wound; that the wound debridement and treatment provided by Tong'an Hospital to Fang Jinkai complied with operating procedures; and that Fang Jinkai engaged in vigorous activity during the recovery period after the second surgery, leading to a re-fracture.

Facts Found by the Tong'an District People's Court of Xiamen City through Trial:

At 12:15 p.m. on July 24, 1998, the plaintiff, Fang Jinkai, was admitted to the First Department of Surgery of the defendant, Tong'an Hospital, after his left leg was mangled by a mixer. The diagnosis was an open fracture of the left tibia and fibula and severe contusion and laceration of the soft tissue of the left leg. At approximately 1:00 p.m. the same day, after Fang Jinkai's relatives signed a consent form, Tong'an Hospital performed a "debridement + internal fixation of the left tibia with a steel plate" and "external fixation of the left leg with a posterior plaster cast." On August 1, Fang Jinkai requested discharge. After劝阻 (dissuasion) failed, and after Fang Jinkai's relatives signed a written statement stating "discharge voluntarily, bear all consequences oneself," Tong'an Hospital processed the discharge procedures.

At 10:25 a.m. on August 1, 1998, the plaintiff, Fang Jinkai, was admitted to the surgical department of Minhai Hospital for treatment. On August 13, Minhai Hospital performed a skin graft on Fang Jinkai. On October 5, they performed an incision expansion, lesion removal, removal of the steel plate, and external fixation with a plaster cast. During the surgery, it was discovered that there was煤砂泥 (coal sediment and mud) remaining in Fang Jinkai's wound.

On October 13, 1998, after being discharged from Minhai Hospital, the plaintiff, Fang Jinkai, was again admitted to the surgical department of the defendant, Tong'an Hospital. The diagnosis was severe open compound injury of the left leg with infection, and fracture of the left tibia and fibula with osteomyelitis. On October 21, during a surgery performed by Tong'an Hospital involving "incision expansion, fracture reduction plus external fixation, and bone grafting," a sequestrum measuring approximately 5 × 3 × 0.3 cm was observed. After surgery, Tong'an Hospital administered comprehensive treatments including anti-inflammatory therapy and drainage, leading to wound healing. Fang Jinkai was discharged on December 24.

On February 11, 1999, the plaintiff, Fang Jinkai, was admitted to the defendant, Tong'an Hospital, for a third time due to pain in his left leg. Physical examination revealed that Fang Jinkai's left leg was deformed with an inward angulation, with "pseudo-joint" activity, a loosened external fixator, a 0.2 × 0.2 cm exudate on the protruding inner side of the left leg with tenderness, positive vertical percussion pain, and the left leg shortened by approximately 2.5 cm compared to the right leg. After anti-inflammatory and infusion therapy, removal of the external fixator, change to a plaster cast fixation, and wound dressing changes, the symptoms and signs improved. Fang Jinkai left the hospital voluntarily on November 6, 2001.

On April 28, 1999, upon the application of the plaintiff, Fang Jinkai, the Tong'an District Medical Accident Appraisal Committee issued an appraisal conclusion that "this does not constitute a medical accident." Fang Jinkai disagreed and applied to the Xiamen Municipal Medical Accident Technical Appraisal Committee for a reappraisal. On May 14, 2002, after appraisal, the Xiamen Municipal Medical Accident Technical Appraisal Committee concluded that: when the patient was admitted to the emergency department, the left leg trauma was severe, the wound was heavily contaminated, the soft tissue was lacerated, the bone ends were exposed, and the medullary cavity contained a large amount of sediment and other contaminants. This was a Type IIIA open fracture, prone to post-operative infection. For treatment of the fracture, external fixation was the appropriate method. The conclusion was: this does not constitute a medical accident.

Upon the application of the defendant, Tong'an Hospital, the court entrusted the Judicial Technical Appraisal Division of the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court to appraise the medical treatment process of the plaintiff, Fang Jinkai. The Forensic Document Review Opinion No. (2002) Xiamen Zhongfa Fayi Zi 154 issued by that division stated: Fang Jinkai's left leg trauma had a large wound surface, severe destruction and contamination of local muscle tissue, open comminuted fracture of the tibia and fibula, and泥沙 (sediment) filling in the medullary cavity of the broken ends. These were intrinsic factors leading to concurrent wound infection and osteomyelitis. Although the hospital performed debridement and internal fixation surgery and other treatments, complications inevitably occurred. After the second surgery for debridement and bone grafting, the osteomyelitis disappeared. However, due to the fusion of the fractured bone ends, the left lower limb became shortened, with partial dysfunction of the ankle joint. Fang Jinkai's disabling consequences were caused by the injury and its complications, and there was no direct causal relationship with the medical treatment. The complications that appeared after Fang Jinkai's injury were directly related to the severe contamination of his wound. Even if the wound debridement had been more thorough at the time, it would have been difficult to guarantee that infection and osteomyelitis would not occur. The treatment measures, principles, and methods adopted by Tong'an Hospital for Fang Jinkai's post-injury treatment complied with medical standards.

During the trial, upon the application of the defendant, Tong'an Hospital, the court permitted orthopedic expert Yang Limin to appear in court as an expert witness. Expert Yang Limin's opinion was: the plaintiff Fang Jinkai's injury was a Type IIIA open fracture, a relatively severe type of fracture, for which it was objectively impossible to achieve complete debridement. The occurrence of osteomyelitis complications was unavoidable. The cause of Fang Jinkai's disability was bone necrosis caused by osteomyelitis, and further, after the second surgery, excessive activity led to a re-fracture, causing the bone ends at the fracture site to overlap by approximately 3 cm. The newly grafted bone could only reinforce the area but could not separate the overlapped portions, thus it could not restore the original length.

The plaintiff, Fang Jinkai, and the defendant, Tong'an Hospital, did not dispute the authenticity and legality of the above evidence and materials, but Fang Jinkai disputed their relevance. He argued that his wound was not objectively impossible to clean thoroughly, but rather that Tong'an Hospital had failed to fulfill its duty during debridement, which caused the bone infection. However, Fang Jinkai was unable to provide supporting evidence for this assertion.

According to the appraisal by the Judicial Technical Appraisal Division of the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court, the plaintiff Fang Jinkai's left lower limb was shortened by 3.3 cm, with a disability grade of Level 9 plus Level 10.

The Tong'an District People's Court of Xiamen City held that there were two points of contention in this case. 1. Whether the wound infection and concurrent osteomyelitis were caused by contaminants in the wound that were objectively impossible to completely remove, or by Tong'an Hospital's subjective fault in failing to perform thorough debridement. 2. Whether there was a direct causal relationship between the bone graft surgery and the leg shortening.

Regarding the first point. After the first surgery, the plaintiff Fang Jinkai's wound still contained some contaminants, and it is an undisputed fact that due to the presence of these contaminants, the wound became infected, leading to osteomyelitis and bone necrosis. Fang Jinkai argued that because he was hospitalized for an open fracture, the wound was open, and the focus of treatment should have been on timely and thorough cleaning of the wound to avoid infection. The fact that the defendant Tong'an Hospital left some contaminants in the wound after debridement, resulting in wound infection, osteomyelitis, and bone necrosis, indicated that the debridement was not performed carefully or thoroughly, and thus the hospital should naturally bear liability for the medical accident. Tong'an Hospital argued that the nature of Fang Jinkai's injury made it impossible to completely remove the contaminants in a single surgery; the fact that after Fang Jinkai underwent a second debridement at another hospital, there were still irremovable coal cinders and other contaminants in the wound was sufficient to prove this point. Our hospital knew that a single surgery could not completely remove the contaminants, and therefore, before the surgery, it informed Fang Jinkai and his relatives of the potential post-operative risks, including post-operative infection, osteomyelitis, etc., and proceeded with the surgery only after obtaining their consent. The hospital's surgical process fully complied with standards, and the outcome was within expectations; therefore, there was no medical accident.

Considering the evidence and respective arguments submitted by both parties, combined with the analysis opinion of the orthopedic expert based on many years of clinical experience and the facts of this case, as well as the forensic document review opinion, it should be determined that: the plaintiff Fang Jinkai's left leg was a Type IIIA open fracture, a relatively severe fracture type, with a large area of trauma, severe destruction and contamination of local muscle tissue, and泥沙 (sediment) filling in the medullary cavity of the broken ends of the tibia and fibula. Objectively, complete debridement was impossible, and this was the direct cause of the post-operative infection and concurrent osteomyelitis. The treatment measures, principles, and methods adopted by the defendant Tong'an Hospital for Fang Jinkai's post-injury treatment complied with medical standards, and there was no medical fault.

Regarding the second point. The plaintiff Fang Jinkai argued that the defendant Tong'an Hospital performed bone graft surgery to treat his fracture, but this procedure caused his left lower limb to be shortened by 3.3 cm, exceeding the upper limit of shortening allowed by medicine, resulting in his disability. Therefore, Tong'an Hospital should be liable for the disabling outcome caused by this surgery. Tong'an Hospital argued that because Fang Jinkai developed wound infection, osteomyelitis, and bone necrosis during treatment, resulting in fusion of the fractured bone ends, and in addition, after his second discharge, he engaged in premature and excessive activity of the affected limb, causing a re-fracture with angulation deformity, his left lower limb was shortened. There was no causal relationship between the left lower limb shortening and the bone graft surgery, and the hospital should not be liable for Fang Jinkai's left lower limb shortening.

Based on the expert opinion and the forensic document review opinion, it should be determined that: the cause of the plaintiff Fang Jinkai's left lower limb shortening was the post-operative infection, osteomyelitis, fusion of the bone ends, and the premature and excessive activity before complete recovery of the affected limb, which led to a re-fracture with angulation deformity, causing the bone ends at the fracture site to overlap. This was unrelated to the bone graft surgery performed by the defendant Tong'an Hospital. The newly grafted bone could only reinforce the healing of the fracture site but could not separate the overlapped bone ends.

In summary, the plaintiff Fang Jinkai sought medical treatment from the defendant Tong'an Hospital after his left leg was mangled by a mixer, and the two parties established a medical service relationship. Upon admission, Fang Jinkai's left leg was not only a relatively severe Type IIIA open fracture but also had a large area of trauma, severe destruction and contamination of local muscle tissue, and泥沙 (sediment) filling in the medullary cavity of the broken ends of the tibia and fibula. According to medical principles, faced with such an injury, Tong'an Hospital had three medical options: first, amputation, which would completely remove contaminants and avoid the risk of post-operative infection, but would undoubtedly cause permanent disability for the patient. Second, extensive resection of contaminated and potentially contaminated soft tissue, which could remove contaminants and minimize the medical risk of post-operative infection to the greatest extent, but would damage the patient's nerves and blood vessels, adversely affecting the patient's future recovery. Third, debridement while preserving bones and soft tissue as much as possible, which would carry the risk of wound infection and concurrent osteomyelitis, but if successful, would be beneficial to the patient's recovery; even if it failed,补救 (remedial) measures such as amputation or extensive soft tissue resection could still be considered. From the perspective of being responsible for the patient, Tong'an Hospital, after obtaining the consent of the patient and his relatives, chose the third option, which carried the greatest risk for the medical staff, and implemented it carefully and prudently. Its treatment measures, steps, and methods all complied with medical standards. The infection after the first surgery was directly related to the complexity of the injury. Furthermore, during the highly infection-prone post-operative period, Fang Jinkai left the hospital voluntarily after signing a statement saying "discharge voluntarily, bear all consequences oneself," which increased the opportunity for infection, leading to his second admission due to concurrent osteomyelitis and bone necrosis. Osteomyelitis, bone necrosis, fusion of the fractured bone ends, and the re-fracture caused by premature and excessive activity after the second surgery were the direct causes of Fang Jinkai's left leg shortening, and were unrelated to Tong'an Hospital's bone graft surgery. The law only pursues liability for damages caused by medical staff's fault in medical practice. Medical treatment is an endeavor with certain risks. The law takes a tolerant attitude towards risky medical procedures implemented by doctors in the interests of patients. If a risky medical procedure is carried out with the consent of the patient and his or her relatives, the risk liability shall be borne by the patient and his or her relatives. Resolving medical disputes based on this principle is conducive to medical staff saving lives and providing relief, conducive to improving their medical skills, and ultimately conducive to the health of patients and the progress of society. Tong'an Hospital had no medical fault in the process of diagnosing and treating Fang Jinkai's leg injury and should not bear liability for compensation. Fang Jinkai's lawsuit requesting Tong'an Hospital to compensate him for lost work income, medical expenses, disability living subsidy, and mental distress damages lacks a factual basis and is not supported.

Accordingly, the Tong'an District People's Court of Xiamen City, in accordance with Article 64, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on October 15, 2002, rendered the following judgment:

Reject all claims of the plaintiff Fang Jinkai.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 3,727 to be borne by the plaintiff Fang Jinkai.

After the judgment was pronounced, Fang Jinkai refused to accept it and appealed to the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province. In addition to insisting on the arguments that there was a direct causal relationship between incomplete debridement and the leg infection and concurrent osteomyelitis, and that the bone graft surgery caused the appellant's left lower limb to shorten beyond the upper limit allowed by medicine, thus the appellee had medical fault and should bear liability for medical accident, the appellant also argued: The appellee was unable throughout the first instance to provide sufficient evidence to prove that there was no causal relationship between its medical treatment and the appellant's damaging consequences. According to the principle of reversed burden of proof, the appellee should bear the consequences of losing the case. However, the first instance found that there was no medical fault on the part of the appellee, which was an error in the application of law. The appellant requested the second instance to reverse the original judgment and enter a judgment in favor of the appellant's claims.

The appellee, Tong'an Hospital, argued in its defense: The judgment of first instance had sufficient factual basis and correct application of law, and should be affirmed. The appellant's appeal was unfounded and should be dismissed.

During the second instance, the appellant Fang Jinkai submitted a "Judicial Appraisal Request," arguing that no newly grafted vital bone was found in the post-operative X-ray films. He requested that the fracture site of the appellant's left leg be incised for appraisal to verify whether the appellee had performed bone graft surgery on the appellant.

Upon trial, the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found and determined in the first instance, and also found: The surgical records of Tong'an Hospital for October 21, 1998, preserved in the case file of the first instance, recorded: "...there was still black dust-like material adhering in the medullary cavity. This piece of bone was removed, and even scraping with a curet or scalpel could not clean off the adherent material. After soaking in 75% alcohol, the contaminants still could not be removed. Considering that this piece of bone was severely contaminated and already showed signs of necrosis, it was decided to remove it (the bone fragment was soaked in 10% formalin solution for future reference). The medullary cavities of the two fractured ends were curetted open, and no granulation tissue was found. Trial reduction was performed under direct vision, and the estimated bone defect was approximately 5 × 3 × 0.8 cm. After re-disinfection and draping of the left iliac region, local anesthesia was administered along the iliac wing, an incision was made, and an iliac bone block approximately 6 × 4 × 1.5 cm was removed. The donor site was coated with bone wax, and after checking for no active oozing, the incision was closed. The removed iliac bone block was trimmed to match the bone defect area and embedded. After checking that the fracture was essentially completely reduced, this position was maintained, and the proximal and distal ends of the fracture were fixed with a single-arm external fixator. Passive movement of the left lower limb was then attempted, and the fracture fixation was found to be secure with good alignment and apposition. Repeated irrigation with hydrogen peroxide disinfectant solution and normal saline was performed. 1.6 million units of sodium penicillin were placed at the fracture site. The remaining iliac bone block was embedded between the fracture ends. After checking for no active oozing, the incision was closed..."

Opinion of the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court:

It is an obvious fact that there is a causal relationship between incomplete debridement in the first surgery and the wound infection complicated by osteomyelitis. In determining whether Tong'an Hospital should bear liability for this, it is necessary not only to examine the causal relationship between the two, but also to identify the reason why Tong'an Hospital was unable to perform the complete debridement duty. As analyzed by several medical experts, given the nature of Fang Jinkai's injury, if the leg was to be saved, it was objectively difficult to achieve complete debridement in a single procedure. "Choose the lesser of two evils, and choose the greater of two goods" is a rational choice when people face a dilemma. Saving the leg was the common expectation of both the hospital and, even more so, the patient. Therefore, when Tong'an Hospital informed Fang Jinkai and his family of the possible complications after the surgery, they still signed the consent form. When the anticipated risk materialized, Fang Jinkai said nothing about his prior willingness to assume that risk, and instead sought to hold the hospital liable solely on the ground that complete debridement was the hospital's duty. Such a ground for litigation is unjustified.

It can be seen from the surgical records quoted above that when the appellee Tong'an Hospital performed the bone grafting surgery on the appellant Fang Jinkai, in addition to the surgeon, there were one first assistant, one second assistant, one nurse, and one anesthesiologist. The recorded entire surgical procedure was smooth and truthful, conformed to operating standards, and was without impropriety. Fang Jinkai has no other basis and only suspects Tong'an Hospital's bone grafting procedure based on the fact that no new bone was found implanted in his post-operative X-ray film. He applied for an exploratory incision to be made on the living body. Such an appraisal is unnecessary, and the application is not accepted. As the experts stated, the osteomyelitis complicated by bone necrosis and the re-fracture caused by excessive post-operative exercise were the reasons for the shortening of Fang Jinkai's left lower limb due to bone overlap. The new bone implanted during the bone grafting procedure could only reinforce the healing of the fracture site and could not separate the overlapping bone ends at the fracture site. There is no causal relationship between the bone grafting procedure and the leg shortening, and Tong'an Hospital cannot be held liable for medical malpractice on this ground.

In summary, after the appellant Fang Jinkai filed this lawsuit for medical injury damages, the appellee Tong'an Hospital has sufficiently proved the facts of the case with ample evidence and has fulfilled its burden of proof. The facts found in the first instance are clear, the law applied is correct, and the judgment is appropriate and should be affirmed. The grounds of appeal raised by Fang Jinkai cannot be established and should be rejected.

Accordingly, the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on December 10, 2002:

The appeal of the appellant Fang Jinkai is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 3,272 shall be borne by the appellant Fang Jinkai.
